compiled_state.title: [brainstorm/preplanning]: operational atomicity check — detect artifact-reference desync patterns in AC generation
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Origin
Placeholder epic converted from bug 0551-3244 (feature request, not defect).

## Problem
Brainstorm and preplanning evaluate features at the capability level but do not surface operational coordination requirements — specifically, the pattern 'Script A creates/updates artifact X, but configuration file Y referencing X is not updated in the same atomic operation.' This gap produced a desync in epic 36a7-dbb5 (plugin release channels) where release.sh created tags + bumped plugin.json but did not update marketplace.json's source.ref in the same run.

## Analogous patterns
- Migration script adding a table without updating a schema registry
- Deployment script bumping a version without updating a manifest referencing it
- Installer adding a plugin entry without updating a required index file

## Proposed scope (not yet brainstormed)
- Operational atomicity check pattern added to brainstorm scrutiny pipeline or preplanning AC generation
- Red-team reviewer (dso:red-team-reviewer) is a candidate insertion point
- For any story touching a script that creates/modifies a versioned artifact, surface the question: 'Is there another file referencing this artifact that must be updated in the same operation?'
- If yes, require explicit AC: '<file> is updated atomically in the same script run/commit as <artifact>.'

## Status
Placeholder — requires /dso:brainstorm session before implementation. Tagged scrutiny:pending.

comments.body:
Scope expansion (2026-04-26, from docs/proposed-mitigations-4-26.md):

Two mitigations absorbed into this epic's atomicity-check scope:

- **G6-M3** — Generalize the operational-atomicity check to also cover known-antipattern audits at brainstorm/preplanning time. When an epic touches a file class associated with a known antipattern (shell hooks → CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT, runners → semantic drift, etc.), inject a pre-emptive task: 'Audit for <antipattern> across all files in scope before implementation begins.' The known-antipattern registry is delivered by New Epic A (static-analysis defense layer) per docs/new-epics-4-26.md; this epic consumes the registry at planning time.
- **G11-M2** — Implementation-plan templated paired sub-task: when a task adds a config key in dso-config.conf or any *.conf, mandatorily emit a paired sub-task documenting the key in CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md (description, type, default, scope, example). Same atomicity pattern as the artifact-desync case (release.sh + marketplace.json that motivated this epic): two artifacts must update together.

Rationale: this epic's existing scope is the artifact-reference desync pattern (Script A creates artifact X, file Y references X but is not updated atomically). Both additions extend the same mechanism to additional artifact pairs (code + antipattern audit; config-key + reference doc). The detection-injection point (red-team-reviewer or AC generation) is the same.

This epic has no children yet (scrutiny:pending); decomposition will pick up the new SCs naturally. Note: tag scrutiny:pending should be cleared once brainstorm runs on this epic.
